plan_a_advantages: Addresses current fatigue state with recovery-focused sessions
Longer trail runs (18km) better simulate trail running distances
Consistent emphasis on recovery and freshness
plan_b_advantages: Includes a dedicated strength and mobility session
Potentially better for building a foundational aerobic base (though this is less critical given the stated goal of speed improvement)
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it addresses a stated state of fatigue and prioritizes recovery. While Plan B includes a tempo run, it’s immediately followed by a rest day, suggesting a focus on building a base rather than pushing towards faster performance. Plan A’s consistent ‘recover and maintain freshness’ purpose summaries and longer, easier runs are more appropriate for an athlete needing to rebuild after fatigue, allowing for a gradual increase in volume and intensity. Furthermore, the longer runs in Plan A (18km) are more aligned with the demands of trail running than the single 122min run in Plan B.
